result.summary: The image depicts a residential street with row houses and a narrow sidewalk that lacks a buffer from the roadway. Pedestrian mobility is hindered by a utility pole placed directly in the walkway, and a driveway or alleyway creates a conflict point on the left.

hazards.name: Utility pole obstruction
hazards.description: A large utility pole is located in the center of the sidewalk, significantly narrowing the effective walking path and creating a barrier for those with mobility aids.

hazards.name: Driveway conflict point
hazards.description: A vehicle access point or alleyway crosses the sidewalk, creating potential for vehicle-pedestrian collisions.

interventions.title: Utility Pole Relocation
interventions.description: Relocate the utility pole to a furniture zone or underground to ensure a clear, ADA-compliant pedestrian path.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Buffer and Street Trees
interventions.description: Install a planting strip or street trees between the sidewalk and the curb to provide physical separation from traffic and improve the pedestrian experience.
